oliver: Heads-up: after switching the edge sample to a single esbuild bundle, generic inference for `client.call<T>()` collapses to `any`. Runtime is fine but CI typecheck fails. Anyone seen bundler + types oddness?

maya: Yes. Often caused by overload fallbacks returning `any` or by different .d.ts being resolved between dev and build. Can you paste a tiny repro?

oliver: Minimal: 
```ts
const r = await client.call<{ name: string }>({ model: 'edge-mini', input: 'hi' });
// expecting r.name to be string, TS infers any after build
```
Types in node_modules show:
```ts
call<T>(opts: CallOpts & { mode: 'typed' }): Promise<T>
call(opts: CallOpts): Promise<any>
```

pras: There's your smoking gun. When TS can't guarantee the first overload across package boundaries it picks the broader `any` return. Two quick fixes: make the fallback generic `call<T = any>(...)` or change fallback to `Promise<unknown>` and provide a small helper to cast.

maya: I prefer `unknown` for public surfaces, but it is breaking. For a fast patch `call<T = any>` preserves inference for current users. Long term we should migrate to `unknown` with a migration note.

oliver: We also had `skipLibCheck: true` in the edge sample tsconfig which hid other declaration mismatches. I'll turn that off in CI to surface issues.

pras: Also check `moduleResolution`/`module` settings. esbuild-based edge samples should use `module: 'ESNext'` + `moduleResolution: 'bundler'`. Node examples should use `node16`/`nodenext`. Mismatches make tsc pick different type entrypoints.

maya: Add a tsd test asserting `call<{ name: string }>` infers `string` so we catch regressions. Also add a dts snapshot that ensures `dist/index.d.ts` contains the typed overload. Rollup/flattening can reorder or inline overloads.

ci-bot: CI types job failure: samples/edge-ts/src/index.ts:14 "Type 'any' is not assignable to type 'string'". See job: https://ci.internal/9999/jobs/11

oliver: Plan: 1) quick PR to make fallback `call<T = any>` so inference preserved, 2) add tsd + dts snapshot tests, 3) align sample tsconfig to bundler resolution and disable skipLibCheck in CI, 4) follow-up RFC to change fallback to `unknown` in a major release with migration notes.

maya: Sounds good. Tag me on the PR and I'll review the types/tests.

pras: If you change public types, include a short changelog note. Unexpected widening/lowering of `any`/`unknown` impacts users.

oliver: Will do. Thanks! :thumbsup:
